summary: This note describes the Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic (TSFSR), a constituent republic of the Soviet Union that existed from 1922 to 1936. It comprised Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia, which were known traditionally as the Transcaucasian Republics because the Caucasus Mountains separated them from Russia. The republic was created ostensibly to consolidate the region's economic situation, but it also helped consolidate Bolshevik control over the states. It was one of the four republics that signed the 1922 treaty establishing the Soviet Union.
one_line: The Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic was a Soviet republic (1922–1936) uniting Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia.
key_facts: The Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic (Transcaucasian SFSR or TSFSR) was a constituent republic of the Soviet Union.
The Transcaucasian SFSR existed from 1922 to 1936.
The Transcaucasian SFSR was also known as the Transcaucasian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic.
The Transcaucasian SFSR comprised Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia.
Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia were known traditionally as the Transcaucasian Republics.
The region was called Transcaucasian because it was separated from Russia by the Caucasus Mountains.
The Transcaucasian SFSR was created ostensibly to consolidate the economic situation of the region.
The Transcaucasian SFSR was also useful in consolidating Bolshevik control over the states.
The Transcaucasian SFSR was one of the four republics to sign the treaty establishing the Soviet Union in 1922.
